phase: K2P+N Z3 injectivity v2 - signed-offset basis fix (this phase)
question: phi(s1) == phi(s2) ==> VAL(s1) == VAL(s2) on every legal pair of a material class - the precondition for replacing states by feature vectors in the MTBDD compiler (sufficient condition for correct compilation; says nothing about ratios)

basis_v1.definition: 5 king (tau, d_AK, opp, e_w, e_b) + 13 knight (nW, nB, k_dist, katt_*, kchk_*, k_*_own/enemy, k_atk_*) [+ 14 pawn] - the basis of every committed compression run

basis_v2.definition: basis_v1 + 8 signed knight offsets (k_dx_w, k_dy_w, k_dx_b, k_dy_b: knight->OWN king; k_dxe_w, k_dye_w, k_dxe_b, k_dye_b: knight->ENEMY king; signed per-axis delta king - piece, -1/-1 when the piece is absent) + 2 king rank-edge distances (re_w, re_b = min(y, N-1-y)) [+ 8 signed pawn offsets (p_dx_*, p_dy_*: pawn->OWN king; p_dxe_*, p_dye_*: pawn->ENEMY king)]
basis_v2.implementation: k2pn_basis.py v2 API (class_features_v2; the v1 API is unchanged) + z3_injectivity.py --basis v2

minimality_ladder.provenance: measured with probe_signed_fix.py + probe2_minimality.py (empirical bucketing over the full classes, no Z3); 'A' = knight->own signed offsets, 'B' = knight->enemy signed offsets, 'C' = king rank-edge distances, 'D' = pawn->own signed offsets, 'E' = pawn->enemy signed offsets, 'O' = opp orientation split
findings: signed knight offsets ALONE (own, enemy, or both) close NO class - the naive fix hypothesis is refuted; every class keeps conflicts
knight-only classes (K+N vs K+N, all N): A or B plus the king rank-edge distances closes ({A,C} = 0 and {B,C} = 0 on kn N=3/4/5); rank-edge is REQUIRED (AB without C still has 8 conflict buckets)
pawn classes: A+B plus signed pawn offsets closes ({A,B,D} = 0 and {A,B,E} = 0 on kpn/mirror/both); the rank-edge pair C is redundant there
the opp orientation split (O: same-file vs same-rank alignment) changes nothing on any class - redundant
the uniform v2 basis (A+B+C+D+E) is therefore mildly overdetermined by design: chosen for a single class-independent definition, not per-class minimality
